subject: Recommended way to create dynamic number of observers?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Recommended way to create dynamic number of observers?
parts:
I've seen similar questions in the past but I haven't seen a satisfactory answer.

To demonstrate, imagine this simple toy app:  There's a numeric input that lets the user decide how many buttons there will be on the page.  Clicking on each button should print out the number of that button.

Here's the "best naive" implementation I could think of:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("num", "Number of buttons", 3),
  uiOutput("buttons")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$buttons <- renderUI({
    lapply(seq_len(input$num), function(x) {
      actionButton(paste0("btn", x), x)
    })
  })
  
  observe({
    lapply(seq_len(input$num), function(x) {
      observeEvent(
        input[[paste0("btn", x)]],
        cat(x)
      )
    })
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

This isn't ideal for two reason: first of all, it seems weird to me to have an observer within an observe.  Is that ok to do?  Second, every time the loop runs, ALL the previous observers that existed get duplicated. For example, if the app starts and we click on the button "2" then the number "2" will get printed once.  But if we change the number of buttons, and then change it again, then that loop will be called two more times, and now there are three observers for the "2" button, so clicking "2" will print it 3 times.

I hope that's clear enough.  Obviously my use cases are more realistic than this, but this seems simple enough to understand

Another approach would be to just pick a very large number and loop once to create a lot of observers, but that's not ideal either.

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: Recommended way to create dynamic number of observers?
parts: Interesting question. I'm not sure there is a 'good' answer but one thing you could do to avoid multiple observers linked to the same button is to name them and then suspend them as needed when the numeric input changes. Perhaps better, if the observers are named I expect you you can check if one already exists for that button and only create new ones as needed (or delete/suspend ones that are no longer needed).
